newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast prods ease after traders spurn API data.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast prods ease after traders spurn API data.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale refined product prices were a shade lower midday Wednesday as traders shrugged off bullish gasoline data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), traders said.
API data released Tuesday showed a sharp 596,000-barrel drop in West Coast (PADD V) gasoline supply last week, in contrast to unexpectedly large nationwide build of 3.6 million.
Wednesday's EIA data reported a dramatically smaller build in gasoline, with supplies up 200,000 barrels.
West Coast spot traders were skeptical of the numbers and buyers withdrew from the market early.
"Nobody believes the draw out here," a traders said. "Our market continues to be weak."
Traders attributed weak spot prices to a 46-cent-a-barrel fall in May crude oil futures and sharp 1.60-cent a gallon slide in front-month unleaded gasoline.

Refinery use continued to rise following the return of plants from spring maintenance last month. Capacity rose 0.3 percentage points last week to 91.3 percent, and with runs much higher, they doubted a drop in gasoline inventories.
CARB regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles fell one cent to 2/73 cents a gallon, with premium steady at 4.50 cents over, players said.
Bay grades were one cent backwardated to L.A. and May barrels in both cities were trading even to April volumes, traders said.
Conventional grade unleaded gasoline also trimmed one cent from Tuesday's late levels to 65.50/66.50 cents.
Distillates were generally one to two cents lower, pressured by a 1.50-cent fall in May heating oil.
